@@ -1,67 +1,67 @@
 PSGlib
 ======
 
 These are all the currently defined functions/macros:
 
 ```
 void PSGPlay (void *song);                              /* this will make your PSG tune start and loop forever */
 void PSGPlayLoops (void *song, unsigned char loops);    /* this will make your PSG tune start and loop the requested amount of times*/
 void PSGPlayNoRepeat (void *song);                      /* this will make your PSG tune start and stop at loop */
 
 void PSGCancelLoop (void);               /* tell the library to stop the tune at next loop */
 void PSGStop (void);                     /* this will make your PSG tune stop (pause) */
 void PSGResume (void);                   /* this will make your stopped (paused) PSG tune resume playing */
 unsigned char PSGGetStatus (void);       /* get the current status of the tune */
 
 PSGSetMusicVolumeChannelsAttenuation (chn0_attenuation,chn1_attenuation,chn2_attenuation,chn3_attenuation)   /* (macro) this will set the tune volume attenuation (0-15) separately for each channel */ 
 PSGSetMusicVolumeAttenuation (attenuation)                                                                   /* (macro) this will set the tune volume attenuation (0-15) evenly for all the channels */
 void PSGSetMusicVolumeChannelsAttenuation_f (unsigned int channels_attenuation);                             /* this is the underlying function for the above macros, and *NOT* meant to be called directly */
 
 void PSGSFXPlay (unsigned char *sfx, unsigned char channels);         /* this will make your SFX start */
 void PSGSFXPlayLoop (unsigned char *sfx, unsigned char channels);     /* this will make your looping SFX start */
 void PSGSFXCancelLoop (void);                                         /* tell the library to stop the SFX at next loop */
 void PSGSFXStop (void);                                               /* this will make your SFX stop */
 unsigned char PSGSFXGetStatus (void);                                 /* get the current status of the SFX */
 
 void PSGSetSFXVolumeAttenuation (unsigned char attenuation);    /* this will set the SFX volume attenuation (0-15) */
 
 void PSGSilenceChannels (void);          /* this will silence all PSG channels */
 void PSGRestoreVolumes (void);           /* this will restore PSG channels volume */
 
 void PSGFrame (void);                    /* you should call this at a constant pace */
 void PSGSFXFrame (void);                 /* you should call this too at a constant pace, if you use SFXs */
 ```
 
 Multibank support
 -----------------
 
 If PSGlib is compiled with PSGLIB_MULTIBANK, the PSGPlay functions
 also take a bank argument. This initial bank is remembered by
 PSGlib and the bank will be switched automatically when calling
 PSGFrame().
 
 PSGlib will automatically switch bank if the song data occupies
 more than 16kB, but it is assumed that the data is not segmented.
 (i.e. it must be consecutive in ROM)
 
 When PSGFrame() returns, the current bank in slot 2 may have
 been changed, so keep this in mind and take the necessary
 steps if necessary. (Set the bank again after the call, or
 use SMS_saveROMBank/restoreROMBank)
 
 When NOT compiled with PSGLIB_MULTIBANK, you must
 set the correct bank before calling PSGFrame manually and
 the song data cannot exceed 16kB.
 
 ```
 /* Only if the library is compiled with PSGLIB_MULTIBANK.
  * Make sure to define PSGLIB_MULTIBANK before including
  * PSGlib.h
  */
 
 void PSGPlay (void *song, unsigned char bank);                              /* this will make your PSG tune start and loop forever */
 void PSGPlayLoops (void *song, unsigned char bank, unsigned char loops);    /* this will make your PSG tune start and loop the requested amount of times*/
 void PSGPlayNoRepeat (void *song, unsigned char bank);                      /* this will make your PSG tune start and stop at loop */
 ```

 void engine_sample_manager_init( const void *psginit ) __naked __z88dk_fastcall
 {
 	( void ) psginit;

 	*/
 	__asm

 		ld bc, #0x0b7f
 		otir

 		__endasm;

 void engine_sample_manager_play( const void *sample )  __naked __z88dk_fastcall
 {
 	( void ) sample;
 
 	/* ********************************************************************
 	Plays a Sample
 	*/
 	__asm
 	; Replayer core to play RLE encoded 8.000kHz samples generated by pcmenc
 		;
 	; pcmenc should use the following command line arguments :
 	;
 	; pcmenc - rto 1 - dt1 12 - dt2 12 - dt3 423 file.wav
 		;
 	; and optionally - r to split sample into blocks for rom replayer
 		;
 
 	; There are three channel updates per underlying sample.
 		; We emit three channel updates together, as fast as possible, looping
 		; every 447 cycles, to match an underlying sample at 8008Hz
 		; ( 3579545 / 447 = 8007.9 ).
 		; Work costs 309 cycles so we waste 139.
 
 
 		PLAY_SAMPLE:
 	; disable interrupts
 		di
 		; save ix
 		push ix
 		ld de, #0x0000
 		ld bc, #0x0000
 		ld a, ( hl )
 		inc hl
 		LDIXLA
 		ld a, ( hl )
 		inc hl
 		LDIXHA
 
 		PsgLoop :
 	; Calculate channel A volume
 		ld a, b; 4
 		sub #0x10; 7
 		jr nc, PsgWaitA; 7 / 12
 		ld a, ( hl ); 7
 		inc hl; 6
 		ld b, a; 4
 		and #0x0f; 7
 		or #0x90; 7
 		LDIYHA; 8 -> 57
 		PsgDoneA:
 
 	; Calculate channel B volume
 		ld a, d; 4
 		sub #0x10; 7
 		jr nc, PsgWaitB; 7 / 12
 		ld a, ( hl ); 7
 		inc hl; 6
 		ld d, a; 4
 		and #0x0f; 7
 		or #0xb0; 7
 		LDIYLA; 8 -> 57
 		PsgDoneB:
 
 	; Calculate channel C volume
 		ld a, e; 4
 		sub #0x10; 7
 		jr nc, PsgWaitC; 7 / 12
 		ld a, ( hl ); 7
 		inc hl; 6
 		ld e, a; 4
 		and #0x0f; 7
 		or #0xd0; 7
 		ld c, a; 4 -> 53
 		PsgDoneC:
 
 	; Output channels
 		push de; 11
 		LDDIYH; 8
 		LDEIYL; 8
 		ld a, c; 4
 		push bc; 11
 		ld c, #0x7f; 7 -> 49
 
 		out( c ), d; 12
 		out( c ), e; 12
 		out( c ), a; 12
 		pop bc; 10
 		pop de; 10 -> 66
 
 		; Waste cycles
 		call Delay
 
 		; Decrement length and return if zero
 		dec ix; 10
 		LDAIXH; 8
 		ORIXL; 8
 		jp nz, PsgLoop; 10 -> 36
 		; restore ix
 		pop ix
 		; enable interrupts
 		ei
 		ret
 
 		PsgWaitA :
 	ld b, a; 4
 		ld a, i; 9
 		ld a, i; 9
 		jr PsgDoneA; 12 -> 34
 
 		PsgWaitB:
 	ld d, a; 4
 		ld a, i; 9
 		ld a, i; 9
 		jr PsgDoneB; 12 -> 34
 
 		PsgWaitC:
 	ld e, a; 4
 		and #0x0; 7
 		and #0x0; 7
 		jr PsgDoneC; 12 -> 30
 
 		Delay:
 	; call Delay 17
 		push bc; 11
 		ld b, #0x6; 7
 		inner_loop: djnz inner_loop; 13 * 5 + 8
 		pop bc; 10
 		in a, ( #0x7f ); 11
 		ret; 10
 		; -- -
 		; 139
 		__endasm;

For completeness, source code was also written in C using the devkitSMS to connect the underlying Z80 code. ###### INSTRUCTIONS Press button 1 to advance through the all screens and press button 2 to go back.
Move joystick Up / Down / Left / Right to select year of record cover to display.
After year select move joystick Left / Right to rotate record cover back / forward. ###### TOOLS - Programming: devkitSMS - Compiler sdcc 3.6 - Languages: C / Z80 - Visual Studio 2015 - Visual Studio Code - Graphics: BMP2Tile 0.43 - Assembler: WLA-DX - Emulators: Emulicious / Fusion / Meka ###### GRAPHICS Original Van Halen record covers images were downloaded and resized using [ResizeImage.net](https://resizeimage.net).
The resized images were then converted to 4bpp using [BMP converter](https://online-converting.com/image/convert2bmp) and finally BMP2Tile. ###### SOURCE CODE https://github.com/SteveProXNA/VanHalenDemoSMS ###### CHEATS Press and hold button 2 on Splash screen to reset year of record cover to display. ###### CREDITS Extra special thanks to: sverx for [devkitSMS](https://github.com/sverx/devkitSMS) and Calindro for the [Emulicious Debugger](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=emulicious.emulicious-debugger)

response.value:
Yes — I think that’s a sensible approach for a **faithful port**. We can use [VanHalenDemoSMS](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/VanHalenDemoSMS) as the organizational model while keeping Transbot’s existing engine and screen divisions. Its [sample manager](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/VanHalenDemoSMS/dev/engine/sample_manager.c) already demonstrates C-callable inline Z80, so the idea fits your established style.

The important distinction is that this would initially be a **hybrid C/assembly port**, not yet a full C rewrite. That’s an advantage: we can preserve understood original behavior while translating and testing one subsystem at a time.

### What needs care

We can’t mechanically put every `.inc` inside a C function:

- **Assembler syntax differs:** Transbot uses WLA-DX; SDCC inline assembly uses its own assembler syntax.
- **Calling conventions matter:** many original routines exchange values in registers or jump into shared code rather than returning like C functions.
- **Memory and interrupts are tightly coupled:** the original uses fixed RAM addresses, its own reset and interrupt vectors, and raster timing. Those must be reconciled with SDCC’s startup and SMSlib, not simply combined.
- **Original sound is custom:** we can initially retain its assembly driver and data. PSGlib can replace it later, but the two should not independently control the PSG at the same time.
- **ROM addresses matter:** some original data contains absolute pointers, so moving it requires relocation or preserving its expected layout.

### Suggested structure

We could create a fresh project modeled on the demo, while keeping the useful test setup:

```text
TransbotC/
  dev/
    main.c
    engine/
    object/
    screen/
    content/
  tests/
  Makefile
  README.md
```

I’d start with a small **vertical slice**: establish the build and module layout, then port startup and the title using carefully adapted assembly routines. Compare the result against the original in Emulicious before moving to input, interrupts, sound, and gameplay. SMSlib APIs can replace original routines where their behavior matches; timing-sensitive code can remain assembly until we understand it.

A matching MD5 is unlikely once SDCC and library startup are introduced, so the target would be **matching behavior and presentation**, validated against the original—not necessarily identical bytes. I wouldn’t replace the current project until we agree on the new baseline.

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 set -euo pipefail
 
 rom=$1
 output=$2
 temporary="${output}.tmp"
 trap 'rm -f "$temporary"' EXIT
 
 expected=dd26c323d1323691fed04cd8498afbcf
 actual=$(md5sum "$rom")
 actual=${actual%% *}
 if [[ $actual != "$expected" ]]; then
     echo "Unexpected ROM checksum for $rom: $actual (expected $expected)" >&2
     exit 1
 fi
 
 emit_asset() {
     local name=$1 offset=$2 length=$3
     printf 'static const unsigned char %s[] = {\n' "$name"
     dd if="$rom" bs=1 skip="$offset" count="$length" status=none | xxd -i
     printf '\n};\n\n'
 }
 
 {
     printf '/* Generated from the verified original ROM. Do not edit. */\n\n'
     emit_asset boot_font 18775 1983
     emit_asset boot_tiles_a 22774 2911
     emit_asset boot_tiles_b 25685 2553
     emit_asset boot_tiles_c 28238 2209
     emit_asset title_tiles 16207 955
     emit_asset title_map 17162 72
     emit_asset title_text 9604 199
 } > "$temporary"
 mv "$temporary" "$output"

`make test` runs **two separate kinds of tests**. Python coordinates them, but only one uses `sz80`:

1. **Python unit tests** — [test_export_assets.py](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/tests/test_export_assets.py) tests the asset exporter’s validation logic directly in Python, including invalid and truncated streams. It does **not** use `sz80`.

2. **Z80 decoder test** — SDCC compiles [test_rle.c](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/tests/test_rle.c) together with the actual inline assembly from [rle_manager.c](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/dev/engine/rle_manager.c). The Python script [run_rle_test.py](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/tests/run_rle_test.py) then launches **`sz80`**, SDCC’s Z80 CPU simulator.

The flow for the second test is:

```text
C test + inline Z80
       ↓ SDCC
test_rle.ihx
       ↓ sz80 executes Z80 instructions
test result written to address $B000
       ↓ Python reads simulator output
pass or fail
```

The C test decodes each of the six original asset streams and compares the output hash with an expected value. Python finds the test’s end address in the linker map, runs the simulator to that point, and checks the result byte.

`sz80` tests the **CPU code**, not the complete Master System display or sound hardware. Emulicious is still needed to check the actual screen and game behavior.

You can run both test groups with:

```sh
cd TransbotCnew
make test
```

The normal `make` build does not require `sz80`; it’s only needed for `make test`.

response.value:
Almost — RLE stands for **Run-Length Encoding**. It’s a simple form of compression: instead of storing a repeated byte many times, you store the byte and the number of times it repeats.

For example, conceptually:

```text
Uncompressed:  00 00 00 00 00 00
Compressed:    repeat 00 six times
```

### What it means in Transbot

Transbot uses its own RLE format for graphics and some tilemap data. The decoder in [rle_manager.c](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/dev/engine/rle_manager.c) understands two kinds of runs:

- **Repeated run:** a count followed by one byte to repeat.
- **Literal run:** a count followed by that many different bytes to copy.

A zero byte ends each stream. For example, a simplified single stream:

```text
04 AA       → AA AA AA AA       repeat AA four times
83 10 20 30 → 10 20 30          copy three literal bytes
00          → end of stream
```

The high bit distinguishes literal runs from repeated runs; the lower seven bits give the count.

### Why the “lanes”?

The original decoder doesn’t write each stream contiguously. It writes one byte, skips ahead by two or four bytes, and then writes the next. It repeats that for each *lane*, producing interleaved output:

```text
Lane 0:  A A B
Lane 1:  X Y Z

Output:  A X A Y B Z
```

This helps compress graphics because corresponding bytes can contain long runs, even if the final interleaved bytes do not. The decoded data is then uploaded to the Master System’s video memory with SMSlib.

### Why use it?

Primarily to **save cartridge ROM space**. Repeated patterns are common in graphics, and the Z80 can decompress this format without needing a complex decoder. The trade-off is that the game must spend time and RAM decompressing the data before displaying it.

The Python runner you tagged, [run_rle_test.py](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/tests/run_rle_test.py), doesn’t perform the decompression itself: it starts `sz80` to execute the actual Z80 decoder and checks the test result.

diff --git a/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/README.md b/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/README.md
index 0000000..0000000 100644
--- a/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/README.md
+++ b/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/README.md
@@ -1,50 +1,50 @@
 # Transbot hybrid C / Z80 port
 
 This is a new, independent vertical slice; `../TransbotC` and `../TransbotASM`
 are not modified. The `dev/engine` and `dev/screen` layout follows the style
 of `../VanHalenDemoSMS`. The goal is to preserve original behavior with
 C-callable assembly first, then replace routines with C/SMSlib selectively.
 
 ## Build and test
 
 Requires SDCC 4.2.0 with `ihx2sms` and `sz80`, Python 3 and make, plus the
 included `../sverx420/devkitSMS` libraries. Run:
 
 ```sh
 cd TransbotCnew
 make test
 make
 ```
 
 Open `build/transbot.sms` in Emulicious or another SMS emulator. `make clean`
 removes generated build files. The build extracts title assets from
 `../TransbotASM/TransBot.sms` after checking its MD5. Do not distribute the
 generated ROM or assets unless you have the necessary rights.
 
 `make test` executes the actual SDCC-assembled decoder in the `sz80` Z80
 simulator and checks independently recorded hashes for all six asset streams.
 The exporter also validates stream boundaries and decoded buffer sizes before
 the unbounded original-style assembly is allowed to consume them.
 
 ## Slice and correspondence
 
 | Original | This project |
 | --- | --- |
 | `engine/vdp_manager.inc`, `$291A` | `dev/engine/rle_manager.c`: Z80 instructions adapted to SDCC syntax, with C-callable 2- and 4-lane entry points. The wrapper preserves IX and uses a relocatable buffer instead of fixed `$D000`. |
 | `engine/boot_manager.inc`, `$2902`, `$28F0`, `$28F6`, `$28FC` | `dev/engine/content_manager.c`: original boot graphics decoded by the assembly routine and uploaded with SMSlib. |
 | `screen/title_screen.inc`, `engine/text_manager.inc` `$255E` | `dev/screen/title_screen.c` and content manager: palette, title graphic and fixed text. |
 | Reset/IRQ/NMI vectors | devkitSMS CRT and SMSlib for now, not the original vector handlers. |
 | Original sound engine | Not ported. PSGlib is linked and silenced; no song is played. Original song bytes are not PSGlib format. |
 
 The title map's second RLE lane continues into the following original ROM
 data before its terminator. The extractor intentionally includes those bytes,
 validates both lanes, and the assembly reproduces the complete decode. Only
 the first 68 words are copied to the screen, as in the original.
 
 This is **not playable**: title timing, score digits, controller transitions,
 demo/gameplay, original sound, reset/pause semantics, and raster IRQ behavior
 remain to be ported. It holds the title indefinitely. Library startup and
 interrupt timing differ from the original, so the resulting ROM is not expected
 to match its MD5. Compare display, timing, input and sound against the original
 in an emulator as later slices are added.

 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 """Extract and validate the specific original ROM streams used by the port."""
 
 import hashlib
 import os
 from pathlib import Path
 import sys
 import tempfile
 
 
 EXPECTED_MD5 = "dd26c323d1323691fed04cd8498afbcf"
 BUFFER_SIZE = 0x0C00
 STREAMS = (
     ("boot_font", 0x4957, 0x5116, (768, 768, 768, 768)),
     ("boot_tiles_a", 0x58F6, 0x6455, (1536, 1536)),
     ("boot_tiles_b", 0x6455, 0x6E4E, (1280, 1280)),
     ("boot_tiles_c", 0x6E4E, 0x76EF, (1280, 1280)),
     ("title_tiles", 0x3F4F, 0x430A, (416, 416, 416, 416)),
     ("title_map", 0x430A, 0x436B, (68, 1274)),
 )
 
 
 def validate_stream(data, lengths):
     pos = 0
     lanes = len(lengths)
     for lane, expected in enumerate(lengths):
         written = 0
         while True:
             if pos >= len(data):
                 raise ValueError("missing lane terminator")
             command = data[pos]
             pos += 1
             if command == 0:
                 break
             count = command & 0x7F
             if count == 0:
                 raise ValueError("invalid zero-length run")
             payload = count if command & 0x80 else 1
             if pos + payload > len(data):
                 raise ValueError("truncated run")
             pos += payload
             written += count
             if (written - 1) * lanes + lane >= BUFFER_SIZE:
                 raise ValueError("stream exceeds decoder buffer")
         if written != expected:
             raise ValueError(f"lane {lane} has {written} bytes, expected {expected}")
     if pos != len(data):
         raise ValueError("unexpected data after final lane")
 
 
 def validate_text(data):
     pos = 1
     if not data or data[0] != 5:
         raise ValueError("invalid title text count")
     for _ in range(data[0]):
         if pos + 4 > len(data):
             raise ValueError("truncated title text header")
         address = int.from_bytes(data[pos:pos + 2], "little")
         size = int.from_bytes(data[pos + 2:pos + 4], "little")
         pos += 4
         if address < 0x3800 or address + size > 0x3F00 or pos + size > len(data):
             raise ValueError("invalid title text bounds")
         pos += size
     if pos != len(data):
         raise ValueError("unexpected trailing title text")
 
 
 def main():
     if len(sys.argv) != 3:
         raise SystemExit("usage: export_assets.py ROM OUTPUT")
     rom = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()
     actual = hashlib.md5(rom).hexdigest()
     if actual != EXPECTED_MD5:
         raise SystemExit(f"Unexpected ROM checksum: {actual} (expected {EXPECTED_MD5})")
 
     assets = []
     for name, start, end, lengths in STREAMS:
         data = rom[start:end]
         try:
             validate_stream(data, lengths)
         except ValueError as error:
             raise SystemExit(f"Invalid {name}: {error}") from error
         assets.append((name, data))
     text = rom[0x2584:0x264B]
     validate_text(text)
     assets.append(("title_text", text))
 
     lines = ["/* Generated from the verified original ROM. Do not edit. */", ""]
     for name, data in assets:
         lines.append(f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{")
         for offset in range(0, len(data), 16):
             lines.append("    " + ", ".join(f"0x{value:02x}" for value in data[offset:offset + 16]) + ",")
         lines.extend(("};", ""))
 
     output = Path(sys.argv[2])
     temporary = None
     try:
         with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", dir=output.parent, delete=False) as file:
             temporary = file.name
             file.write("\n".join(lines))
         os.replace(temporary, output)
     finally:
         if temporary and os.path.exists(temporary):
             os.unlink(temporary)
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     main()

It comes from tracing the original disassembly and ROM data—not from the label alone.

### Why `$2519` is recorded-input playback

In [input_manager.inc](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotASM/engine/input_manager.inc:2), the input update checks a flag and, when bit 3 is set, jumps to [_LABEL_2519_](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotASM/engine/input_manager.inc:149) instead of reading the controller ports.

The demo setup in [game_screen.inc](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotASM/screen/game_screen.inc:19) sets that flag and copies five initial state bytes into RAM. Those bytes are in [vector_manager.inc](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotASM/engine/vector_manager.inc:51):

```asm
.db $02 $00 $00 $80 $7A
```

The last two bytes form the little-endian pointer **`$7A80`**. At `$2519`, the routine reads from that pointer and writes the input value to `_RAM_C10C_`, the same input location used for the player.

### Why 1,516 frames

The data at `$7A80` is a sequence of **duration, input** byte pairs, ending with a zero duration. The routine applies each input for the specified number of updates. Its first pairs are:

```text
0C 00   → input $00 for 12 updates
0D 08   → input $08 for 13 updates
0B 09   → input $09 for 11 updates
02 08   → input $08 for 2 updates
```

I summed all the duration bytes up to the terminator at `$7C9A`: **269 pairs, totaling 1,516 input updates**. The update routine is called from the VBlank handler, so those correspond to 1,516 VBlank frames during uninterrupted playback.

The test in [test_demo.c](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/tests/test_demo.c) checks that full sequence, then checks that the following update detects the terminator. It tests the input stream—not yet the rendered gameplay.

void engine_content_manager_load_boot_tiles(void)
{
    engine_rle_decode_4(boot_font);
    SMS_VRAMmemcpy(0x2000, engine_rle_buffer, 0x0c00);
    engine_rle_decode_2(boot_tiles_a);
    SMS_VRAMmemcpy(0x0000, engine_rle_buffer, 0x0c00);
    engine_rle_decode_2(boot_tiles_b);
    SMS_VRAMmemcpy(0x0c00, engine_rle_buffer, 0x0a00);
    engine_rle_decode_2(boot_tiles_c);
    SMS_VRAMmemcpy(0x1600, engine_rle_buffer, 0x0a00);
}

void engine_content_manager_load_title(void)
{
    const unsigned char *text = title_text;
    unsigned char count;
    unsigned char row;

    SMS_loadBGPalette(title_bg_palette);
    SMS_loadSpritePalette(title_sprite_palette);
    engine_rle_decode_4(title_tiles);
    SMS_VRAMmemcpy(0x2c00, engine_rle_buffer, 0x0680);

    engine_rle_decode_2(title_map);
    for (row = 0; row < 4; ++row)
        SMS_VRAMmemcpy(0x398e + (unsigned int)row * 64,
                       engine_rle_buffer + (unsigned int)row * 34, 34);

    count = *text++;
    while (count--) {
        unsigned int address = text[0] | ((unsigned int)text[1] << 8);
        unsigned int size = text[2] | ((unsigned int)text[3] << 8);
        text += 4;
        SMS_VRAMmemcpy(address, text, size);
        text += size;
    }
}

I checked this with an auto-start build of the same code, in a scratch folder I've since deleted; I didn't test pressing a button on the title screen to enter the game. **RAM layout**
- The link now uses `--data-loc 0xC620`, so SMSlib and SDCC variables sit above the original's fixed `$C000–$C61F` block. I confirmed this in the map file.
- `engine_rle_buffer` is fixed at `$D000`, where the original scroll tables expect it.
- `original_ram.h` names the original variables that the C code touches.

**Scroll engine**
- **Converter:** `tools/port_asm.py` converts the original WLA routines to SDCC assembler. These are the scroll manager, the `$2D01–$2D6F` block, the VDP helpers and the VBlank column streaming.

- **ASM quirk:** the original writes `ld hl,_DATA_8_` and `ld de,_DATA_F_` to mean the numbers 8 and 15. The converter emits plain numbers for those. It's noted in the README.
- **Interrupts:** [game_screen.c](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/dev/screen/game_screen.c) ports the `$0FA6` frame and line scroll-register writes to SMSlib's frame and line interrupt hooks. The line counter is `$7F`, as in the original.
- **Entering the game:** pressing button 1 or 2 on the title now starts this scrolling background. The main loop in `main.c` calls the scroll update each frame afterwards.

**Not ported yet:**
- Objects, the player and HUD.

 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 """Run the compiled Z80 decoder tests in the SDCC simulator."""
 
 from pathlib import Path
 import re
 import subprocess
 import sys
 
 
 def run_test(simulator, ihx, map_file, name):
     map_text = Path(map_file).read_text()
     match = re.search(r"^\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s+_test_done\s", map_text, re.MULTILINE)
     if not match:
         raise SystemExit("Cannot find test_done in linker map")
     address = int(match.group(1), 16)
     commands = f"run 0 0x{address:x}\ndump /x rom 0xe000 0xb000\nquit\n"
     result = subprocess.run(
         [simulator, "-q", "-c", "-", ihx],
         input=commands, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60, check=True,
     )
     stop = re.search(r"^Stop at 0x([0-9a-fA-F]+):.*Breakpoint", result.stdout, re.MULTILINE)
     if not stop or int(stop.group(1), 16) != address:
         raise SystemExit(f"Simulator did not reach test_done:\n{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")
     match = re.search(r"^0x0*e000\s+([0-9a-fA-F]{2})\b", result.stdout, re.MULTILINE)
     if not match:
         raise SystemExit(f"Could not read simulator test result:\n{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")
     code = int(match.group(1), 16)
     if code:
         raise SystemExit(f"Z80 {name} test failed at checkpoint {code}:\n{result.stdout}")
     print(f"Z80 {name} test passed")
 
 
 def main():
     simulator, ihx, map_file = sys.argv[1:]
     run_test(simulator, ihx, map_file, "RLE")
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     main()

 # Transbot hybrid C / Z80 port
 
 This is a new, independent vertical slice; `../TransbotC` and `../TransbotASM`
 are not modified. The `dev/engine` and `dev/screen` layout follows the style
 of `../VanHalenDemoSMS`. The goal is to preserve original behavior with
 C-callable assembly first, then replace routines with C/SMSlib selectively.
 
 ## Build and test
 
 Requires SDCC 4.2.0 with `ihx2sms` and `sz80`, Python 3 and make, plus the
 included `../sverx420/devkitSMS` libraries. Run:
 
 ```sh
 cd TransbotCnew
 make test
 make
 ```
 
 Open `build/transbot.sms` in Emulicious or another SMS emulator. `make clean`
 removes generated build files. The build extracts title assets from
 `../TransbotASM/TransBot.sms` after checking its MD5. Do not distribute the
 generated ROM or assets unless you have the necessary rights.
 
 `make test` executes the actual SDCC-assembled decoder in the `sz80` Z80
 simulator and checks independently recorded hashes for all six asset streams.
 The exporter also validates stream boundaries and decoded buffer sizes before
 the unbounded original-style assembly is allowed to consume them.
 It also runs the assembled recorded-demo-input routine against boundary cases
 and the full 1,516-frame original input stream.
 
 ## Slice and correspondence
 
 | Original | This project |
 | --- | --- |
 | `engine/vdp_manager.inc`, `$291A` | `dev/engine/rle_manager.c`: Z80 instructions adapted to SDCC syntax, with C-callable 2- and 4-lane entry points. The wrapper preserves IX and uses a relocatable buffer instead of fixed `$D000`. |
 | `engine/boot_manager.inc`, `$2902`, `$28F0`, `$28F6`, `$28FC` | `dev/engine/content_manager.c`: original boot graphics decoded by the assembly routine and uploaded with SMSlib. |
 | `screen/title_screen.inc`, `engine/text_manager.inc` `$255E` | `dev/screen/title_screen.c` and content manager: palette, title graphic and fixed text. |
 | `engine/screen_manager.inc` `$0429` (scroll-related half) | `dev/screen/game_screen.c`: palette, stage sprite tiles (`$5116`), stage map decoded to the fixed buffer at `$D000` (`$4446`), cleared name table/SAT, original RAM block cleared. Press button 1/2 on the title to enter: the stage-1 background scrolls. No objects, HUD or input yet. |
 | `engine/scroll_manager.inc` `$2957-$2D00`, `$2D01-$2D6F`, VDP helpers `$27F7`, `$285B`, VBlank column streaming from `engine/interrupt_manager.inc` | `dev/engine/scroll_manager_z80.s`: **generated** from the original by `tools/port_asm.py` (WLA to sdasz80 syntax). `make test` assembles it at the original addresses and requires every byte to equal the ROM, and that the checked-in file is up to date. `dev/engine/scroll_manager.c` wraps it; `game_screen.c` ports the `$0FA6` VBlank/line scroll-register writes to SMSlib interrupt hooks. |
 | `engine/input_manager.inc` `$2519`, `screen/game_screen.inc` `$0347` | `dev/engine/demo_input_manager.c`: original recorded-input logic, with relocatable state and stream. Tested independently, not yet connected to the ROM's main loop. |
 | Reset/IRQ/NMI vectors | devkitSMS CRT and SMSlib for now, not the original vector handlers. |
 | Original sound engine | Not ported. PSGlib is linked and silenced; no song is played. Original song bytes are not PSGlib format. |
 
 The title map's second RLE lane continues into the following original ROM
 data before its terminator. The extractor intentionally includes those bytes,
 validates both lanes, and the assembly reproduces the complete decode. Only
 the first 68 words are copied to the screen, as in the original.
 
 This is **not playable**: title timing, score digits, controller transitions,
 gameplay objects/HUD/collision and the stage sequencer, original sound, reset/pause semantics,
 and raster IRQ behavior remain to be ported. The input playback code is not
 linked into the title-only ROM yet: the demo requires the original gameplay
 object, map, collision and input routines as well. It holds the
 title indefinitely. Library startup and
 interrupt timing differ from the original, so the resulting ROM is not expected
 to match its MD5. Compare display, timing, input and sound against the original
 in an emulator as later slices are added.
 
 ## RAM layout
 
 The ported original routines use fixed RAM (`$C000-$C61F` variables, `$D000`
 decode buffer). The link uses `--data-loc 0xC620` so SDCC and SMSlib variables

 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 """Extract the recorded demo input from the verified original ROM.
 
 The graphics and code come straight from the converted original assembly, so the
 demo stream (which has no label in the disassembly) is the only exported asset."""
 
 import hashlib
 import os
 from pathlib import Path
 import sys
 import tempfile
 
 
 EXPECTED_MD5 = "dd26c323d1323691fed04cd8498afbcf"
 
 
 def validate_demo(data):
     if len(data) != 539 or data[-1] != 0:
         raise ValueError("incorrect demo stream length or terminator")
     for pos in range(0, len(data) - 1, 2):
         if not data[pos] or data[pos + 1] & 0xC0:
             raise ValueError(f"invalid demo input pair at offset {pos}")
 
 
 def main():
     if len(sys.argv) != 3:
         raise SystemExit("usage: export_assets.py ROM OUTPUT")
     rom = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()
     actual = hashlib.md5(rom).hexdigest()
     if actual != EXPECTED_MD5:
         raise SystemExit(f"Unexpected ROM checksum: {actual} (expected {EXPECTED_MD5})")
 
     demo = rom[0x7A80:0x7C9B]
     validate_demo(demo)
     assets = [("demo_input", demo)]
 
     lines = ["/* Generated from the verified original ROM. Do not edit. */", ""]
     for name, data in assets:
         lines.append(f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{")
         for offset in range(0, len(data), 16):
             lines.append("    " + ", ".join(f"0x{value:02x}" for value in data[offset:offset + 16]) + ",")
         lines.extend(("};", ""))
 
     output = Path(sys.argv[2])
     temporary = None
     try:
         with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", dir=output.parent, delete=False) as file:
             temporary = file.name
             file.write("\n".join(lines))
         os.replace(temporary, output)
     finally:
         if temporary and os.path.exists(temporary):
             os.unlink(temporary)
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     main()

  tiles come from VRAM `$0000`. SMSlib defaults to `$2000` (the boot font), so

  original ran with its own interrupt timing. Under SMSlib an interrupt between
  the two bytes of a VDP command corrupted registers (the player sprite turned
  into font letters), so `screen_game_screen_update()` runs with interrupts
  masked.
- ROM pointers that the original compared as literals (`$2B49`, `$2C0B`) are
  rewritten to symbols by the converter, since the code is relocated.

**Headless emulator check.** Genesis Plus GX does emulate the Master System, and I used it through `~/.copilot/session-state/…/files/sms_probe.c` to run the ROM without opening a window. It reads the game's RAM and writes screenshots at chosen frames.

**What was wrong:**
1. **Wrong sprite tile base.** The original game sets VDP register 6 to `$FB`, so sprite tiles come from VRAM `$0000`. SMSlib defaults to `$2000`, where the boot font is stored. I now write `$FB` in `screen_game_screen_load()` in `game_screen.c`.
2. **An interrupt race.** After that fix the ship was right at first, then turned into letters. The six tile numbers `0c,05,00,06,07,0a` spell `L,E,space,F,G,J` in the font's order, so register 6 had been reset to `$FF`. The original object code writes to the VDP from the main loop. If SMSlib's interrupt landed between the two bytes of a VDP command, the registers were corrupted. Masking interrupts around `screen_game_screen_update()` fixed it, and the ship is still correct at frame 898.

I also fixed two relocated pointers (`$2B49` and `$2C0B`) in the converter, and set up the original's interrupt-disabled setup sequence.

**Caveats and open items:**
- Interrupts are now off for the whole update. If it ever runs longer than a frame, the line-interrupt scroll split could jitter. I haven't measured the update time. The cleaner fix is to mask interrupts only around the VDP writes.

The ROM is now 32 KB like the original. The 48 KB came from my putting the graphics in a separate bank 2, and I've removed that along with the bank switching.

**Problems found and fixed on the way:**
1. **Overlap with the SEGA header.** At 32 KB, the startup code landed on top of the header at `$7FF0`, which would have broken the cartridge. The tests didn't catch it, so I added a check that the ROM is 32,768 bytes and that the header still reads `TMR SEGA`. To make room I dropped PSGlib and replaced it with the same four PSG-mute writes the original boot code uses. Audio was already deferred. The original's sound engine isn't PSGlib format, so I plan to port it as Z80 code.
2. **A hang at around 10 seconds of play, which is probably why the enemy graphics looked wrong.** Enemy code loads its animation tables by their original ROM addresses, for example `ld hl,$1FD6`. Once the code was relocated, those addresses pointed at unrelated bytes. In the first 48 KB build this happened to work by luck. After the change the game hung with RAM full of `0x3f`. The converter in `port_asm.py` now turns the 15 table addresses (`DATA_POINTERS`) into label references, including ones into the middle of a table. A new test, `tests/test_relocation.py`, fails if a numeric address comes back.

**Results.**
- `make test all` passes, including the byte-for-byte check of the converted code against the original ROM.
- The ROM is 31,068 bytes used of 32,768.
- A 30-second headless run (1,800 frames, no input) has no hang. Red spiked mines now fly in at about 14 seconds, and the player ship, HUD and parallax all look right.
- I did not run it in Emulicious or on real hardware.

**Next steps.** The next steps are to test player movement and firing with injected button presses, and to check the interrupt masking around the main-loop update on frame timing. Tell me which you'd like to do first.

  hardware. Check with a random-RAM start when changing startup code.

  tables such as `$1FD6`, listed in `DATA_POINTERS`) are rewritten to symbols by

I've fixed both problems and rebuilt `build/transbot.sms`. I couldn't run Emulicious or Kega Fusion here, so please re-test on both. My checks used the Genesis Plus GX core with random power-on RAM, and `make test all` passes.

**Black screen on Emulicious**
- **Cause:** the devkit startup code only clears about 254 bytes of RAM from `$C000`. I had moved the SDCC variables up to `$C620` to leave room for the original game's RAM, so SMSlib's own variables were never cleared. That includes the interrupt handler pointers. Emulators that zero RAM hid this. Emulicious and real hardware don't, so the first interrupt jumped to a garbage address.
- **Fix:** I added `dev/crt0_sms.s`, a copy of the devkit startup file whose only change is clearing `$C000–$DFEE`. The Makefile builds and links it.
- **Test:** I filled RAM with random bytes before power-on and ran six seeds. All six boot to identical frames.

**Black tiles in the background (Kega Fusion)**
- **Cause:** the sprite upload used SMSlib's `SMS_VRAMmemcpy`, which turns interrupts back on inside my frame handler. The original handler keeps them off. A line interrupt could then fire in the middle of the first screen draw and corrupt the VDP address. That dropped name-table cells.
- **Evidence:** VRAM dumps showed five cells still holding the clear value (row 17 columns 21–23, row 23 columns 30–31) in my ROM but not in the original.
- **Fix:** the handler now uses plain port writes for the sprite table. The black cells are gone at the first frames and at later frames.
- **Related change:** this was probably also what turned the player sprite into letters earlier. With it fixed, I removed the `di`/`ei` I had added around the main-loop update. Frame output is identical with and without it.

**What the test run shows**
- The ROM is still 32 KB (31,092 bytes used) and the SEGA header is intact.
- In a 30-second headless run with no input, the player is hit by enemies. The score reaches 400, a life is lost, and "PLAYER-1 START" appears again. Gameplay is running.
- The README now documents the startup RAM clear and the interrupt finding.

If either emulator still misbehaves, tell me which one and what you see. Emulicious would be the more useful report, because it's the one I can't check here.

response.value:
Yes—**it was added to clear more RAM**, because Transbot uses an unusual RAM layout.

Normally, devkitSMS places its C variables starting at `$C000`. Its existing `crt0_sms.rel` is the assembled startup code, so you don't need the `.s` source in a typical project.

For Transbot, we reserved `$C000–$C61F` for the original game's fixed-address variables and moved SDCC/SMSlib variables to `$C620`. The stock startup code still begins clearing at `$C000` and clears only `l__DATA` bytes. In this build, that didn't reach the relocated SMSlib variables—including interrupt-handler pointers.

I therefore copied the startup source into [crt0_sms.s](/home/stevepro/Steven/Code/testing2/TransbotCnew/dev/crt0_sms.s), changed the clear length, and had the Makefile assemble it into the `.rel` file used by Transbot. Your devkitSMS copy is unchanged.

**One correction:** the comment in the project copy says it clears through `$DFEE`, but the actual instruction clears through **`$DEEE`**. That is still enough to clear the relocated variables and the original game's work RAM. My earlier explanation repeated the incorrect comment; sorry about that. Also, the random-RAM test supported this as the cause of the Emulicious startup issue, but I haven't independently confirmed it in Emulicious.

@@ -1,101 +1,101 @@
 # Transbot hybrid C / Z80 port
 
 This is a new, independent vertical slice; `../TransbotC` and `../TransbotASM`
 are not modified. The `dev/engine` and `dev/screen` layout follows the style
 of `../VanHalenDemoSMS`. The goal is to preserve original behavior with
 C-callable assembly first, then replace routines with C/SMSlib selectively.
 
 ## Build and test
 
 Requires SDCC 4.2.0 with `ihx2sms` and `sz80`, Python 3 and make, plus the
 included `../sverx420/devkitSMS` libraries. Run:
 
 ```sh
 cd TransbotCnew
 make test
 make
 ```
 
 Open `build/transbot.sms` in Emulicious or another SMS emulator. `make clean`
 removes generated build files. The build extracts title assets from
 `../TransbotASM/TransBot.sms` after checking its MD5. Do not distribute the
 generated ROM or assets unless you have the necessary rights.
 
 `make test` executes the actual SDCC-assembled decoder in the `sz80` Z80
 simulator and checks independently recorded hashes for all six asset streams.
 The exporter also validates stream boundaries and decoded buffer sizes before
 the unbounded original-style assembly is allowed to consume them.
 It also runs the assembled recorded-demo-input routine against boundary cases
 and the full 1,516-frame original input stream.
 
 ## Slice and correspondence
 
 | Original | This project |
 | --- | --- |
 | `engine/vdp_manager.inc`, `$291A` | `dev/engine/rle_manager.c`: Z80 instructions adapted to SDCC syntax, with C-callable 2- and 4-lane entry points. The wrapper preserves IX and uses a relocatable buffer instead of fixed `$D000`. |
 | `engine/boot_manager.inc`, `$2902`, `$28F0`, `$28F6`, `$28FC` | `dev/engine/content_manager.c`: original boot graphics decoded by the assembly routine and uploaded with SMSlib. |
 | `screen/title_screen.inc`, `engine/text_manager.inc` `$255E` | `dev/screen/title_screen.c` and content manager: palette, title graphic and fixed text. |
 | `engine/screen_manager.inc` `$0429` (scroll-related half) | `dev/screen/game_screen.c`: palette, stage sprite tiles (`$5116`), stage map decoded to the fixed buffer at `$D000` (`$4446`), cleared name table/SAT, original RAM block cleared. Press button 1/2 on the title to enter: the stage-1 background scrolls. No objects, HUD or input yet. |
 | `engine/scroll_manager.inc` `$2957-$2D00`, `$2D01-$2D6F`, VDP helpers `$27F7`, `$285B`, VBlank column streaming from `engine/interrupt_manager.inc` | `dev/engine/scroll_manager_z80.s`: **generated** from the original by `tools/port_asm.py` (WLA to sdasz80 syntax). `make test` assembles it at the original addresses and requires every byte to equal the ROM, and that the checked-in file is up to date. `dev/engine/scroll_manager.c` wraps it; `game_screen.c` ports the `$0FA6` VBlank/line scroll-register writes to SMSlib interrupt hooks. |
 | `engine/input_manager.inc` `$2519`, `screen/game_screen.inc` `$0347` | `dev/engine/demo_input_manager.c`: original recorded-input logic, with relocatable state and stream. Tested independently, not yet connected to the ROM's main loop. |
 | Reset/IRQ/NMI vectors | devkitSMS CRT and SMSlib for now, not the original vector handlers. |
 | Original sound engine | Not ported. PSGlib is not linked (the ROM must fit in 32 KB like the original); the PSG is muted at start. Original song bytes are not PSGlib format, so the original sound engine will be ported as Z80 code. |
 
 The title map's second RLE lane continues into the following original ROM
 data before its terminator. The extractor intentionally includes those bytes,
 validates both lanes, and the assembly reproduces the complete decode. Only
 the first 68 words are copied to the screen, as in the original.
 
 This is **not playable**: title timing, score digits, controller transitions,
 gameplay objects/HUD/collision and the stage sequencer, original sound, reset/pause semantics,
 and raster IRQ behavior remain to be ported. The input playback code is not
 linked into the title-only ROM yet: the demo requires the original gameplay
 object, map, collision and input routines as well. It holds the
 title indefinitely. Library startup and
 interrupt timing differ from the original, so the resulting ROM is not expected
 to match its MD5. Compare display, timing, input and sound against the original
 in an emulator as later slices are added.
 
 ## RAM layout
 
 The ported original routines use fixed RAM (`$C000-$C61F` variables, `$D000`
 decode buffer). The link uses `--data-loc 0xC620` so SDCC and SMSlib variables
 sit above the original block, and `engine_rle_buffer` is fixed at `$D000`
 (`dev/engine/original_ram.h` names the original variables used from C).
 In the original, `ld hl, _DATA_8_`/`ld de, _DATA_F_` use ROM addresses as the
 literals 8 and 15; the converter emits those as plain numbers.
 
 ## Gameplay (object system) slice
 
 `tools/port_asm.py convert` turns the original gameplay files (objects, stage,
 map, scroll, score, collision, graphics data) into `build/original_game.s`,
 which is linked with the C code; `dev/engine/original_game.h` declares it. The
 graphics data is linked right after the code, so the ROM is 32 KB like the
 original (no bank switching). `game_screen.c`
 runs the original per-frame routines from the SMSlib frame interrupt and the
 main loop.
 
 Findings worth keeping:
 
 - The original init table (`$003B`) sets VDP register 6 to `$FB`, so sprite
   tiles come from VRAM `$0000`. SMSlib defaults to `$2000` (the boot font), so
   `screen_game_screen_load()` writes `$FB` to register 6.
 - The original VBlank handler keeps interrupts disabled until its final `ei`. SMSlib
   helpers such as `SMS_VRAMmemcpy` re-enable them, which let a line interrupt hit the
   middle of the display-off screen draw and drop name-table cells (black tiles) and,
   later, corrupt VDP registers (the player sprite turned into font letters). The
   frame handler in `game_screen.c` therefore uses plain port writes only.
 - `dev/crt0_sms.s` is the devkitSMS startup file with one change: it clears all work
   RAM (`$C000-$DFEE`). The stock file clears only `l__DATA` bytes from `$C000`, which
   missed SMSlib's variables (handler pointers) once `--data-loc` moved to `$C620`.
   That worked on emulators that zero RAM but halted on Emulicious and would on
   hardware. Check with a random-RAM start when changing startup code.
 - ROM addresses used as literals (`$2B49`, `$2C0B`, and the inline enemy animation
   tables such as `$1FD6`, listed in `DATA_POINTERS`) are rewritten to symbols by
   the converter, since the code is relocated. Leaving them as numbers made enemies
   read random ROM bytes and hung the game.
 - `ihx2sms` warns when the ROM exceeds 32 KB; check the `_GSINIT` area in
   `build/transbot.map` ends below `$7FF0`, which `tests/test_rom_assets.py` also checks.
 - `make test` also checks the stage streams inside the built ROM against the
   original and runs the original decoders and scroll setup in `sz80`.

 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 """Run the compiled Z80 decoder tests in the SDCC simulator."""
 
 from pathlib import Path
 import re
 import subprocess
 import sys
 
 
 def run_test(simulator, ihx, map_file, name):
     map_text = Path(map_file).read_text()
     match = re.search(r"^\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s+_test_done\s", map_text, re.MULTILINE)
     if not match:
         raise SystemExit("Cannot find test_done in linker map")
     address = int(match.group(1), 16)
     commands = f"run 0 0x{address:x}\ndump /x rom 0xe000 0xb000\nquit\n"
     result = subprocess.run(
         [simulator, "-q", "-c", "-", ihx],
         input=commands, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60, check=True,
     )
     stop = re.search(r"^Stop at 0x([0-9a-fA-F]+):.*Breakpoint", result.stdout, re.MULTILINE)
     if not stop or int(stop.group(1), 16) != address:
         raise SystemExit(f"Simulator did not reach test_done:\n{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")
     match = re.search(r"^0x0*e000\s+([0-9a-fA-F]{2})\b", result.stdout, re.MULTILINE)
     if not match:
         raise SystemExit(f"Could not read simulator test result:\n{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")
     code = int(match.group(1), 16)
     if code:
         raise SystemExit(f"Z80 {name} test failed at checkpoint {code}:\n{result.stdout}")
     print(f"Z80 {name} test passed")
 
 
 def main():
     simulator, ihx, map_file = sys.argv[1:]
     run_test(simulator, ihx, map_file, "RLE")
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     main()

 # Transbot hybrid C / Z80 port
 
 This is a new, independent vertical slice; `../TransbotC` and `../TransbotASM`
 are not modified. The `dev/engine` and `dev/screen` layout follows the style
 of `../VanHalenDemoSMS`. The goal is to preserve original behavior with
 C-callable assembly first, then replace routines with C/SMSlib selectively.
 
 ## Build and test
 
 Requires SDCC 4.2.0 with `ihx2sms` and `sz80`, Python 3 and make, plus the
 included `../sverx420/devkitSMS` libraries. Run:
 
 ```sh
 cd TransbotCnew
 make test
 make
 ```
 
 Open `build/transbot.sms` in Emulicious or another SMS emulator. `make clean`
 removes generated build files. The build extracts title assets from
 `../TransbotASM/TransBot.sms` after checking its MD5. Do not distribute the
 generated ROM or assets unless you have the necessary rights.
 
 `make test` executes the actual SDCC-assembled decoder in the `sz80` Z80
 simulator and checks independently recorded hashes for all six asset streams.
 The exporter also validates stream boundaries and decoded buffer sizes before
 the unbounded original-style assembly is allowed to consume them.
 It also runs the assembled recorded-demo-input routine against boundary cases
 and the full 1,516-frame original input stream.
 
 ## Slice and correspondence
 
 | Original | This project |
 | --- | --- |
 | `engine/vdp_manager.inc`, `$291A` | `dev/engine/rle_manager.c`: Z80 instructions adapted to SDCC syntax, with C-callable 2- and 4-lane entry points. The wrapper preserves IX and uses a relocatable buffer instead of fixed `$D000`. |
 | `engine/boot_manager.inc`, `$2902`, `$28F0`, `$28F6`, `$28FC` | `dev/engine/content_manager.c`: original boot graphics decoded by the assembly routine and uploaded with SMSlib. |
 | `screen/title_screen.inc`, `engine/text_manager.inc` `$255E` | `dev/screen/title_screen.c` and content manager: palette, title graphic and fixed text. |

Press button 1/2 on the title to enter: the stage-1 background scrolls. No objects, HUD or input yet. |

 The title map's second RLE lane continues into the following original ROM
 data before its terminator. The extractor intentionally includes those bytes,
 validates both lanes, and the assembly reproduces the complete decode. Only
 the first 68 words are copied to the screen, as in the original.
 
 This is **not playable**: title timing, score digits, controller transitions,
 gameplay objects/HUD/collision and the stage sequencer, original sound, reset/pause semantics,
 and raster IRQ behavior remain to be ported. The input playback code is not
 linked into the title-only ROM yet: the demo requires the original gameplay
 object, map, collision and input routines as well. It holds the
 title indefinitely. Library startup and
 interrupt timing differ from the original, so the resulting ROM is not expected
 to match its MD5. Compare display, timing, input and sound against the original
 in an emulator as later slices are added.
 
 ## RAM layout
 
 The ported original routines use fixed RAM (`$C000-$C61F` variables, `$D000`
 decode buffer). The link uses `--data-loc 0xC620` so SDCC and SMSlib variables
 sit above the original block, and `engine_rle_buffer` is fixed at `$D000`
 (`dev/engine/original_ram.h` names the original variables used from C).
 In the original, `ld hl, _DATA_8_`/`ld de, _DATA_F_` use ROM addresses as the
 literals 8 and 15; the converter emits those as plain numbers.
 
 ## Gameplay (object system) slice
 
 `tools/port_asm.py convert` turns the original gameplay files (objects, stage,
 map, scroll, score, collision, graphics data) into `build/original_game.s`,
 which is linked with the C code; `dev/engine/original_game.h` declares it. The
 graphics data is linked right after the code, so the ROM is 32 KB like the
 original (no bank switching). `game_screen.c`
 runs the original per-frame routines from the SMSlib frame interrupt and the
 main loop.
 
 Gameplay initialization sets the original secret-command flags at `$C100` to
 `$0F` after clearing RAM and before screen setup. This enables all four flags,
 equivalent to replacing the original load from `$C012` with `ld a, $0f; nop`.
 The secret-select screen itself is not included.
 
 Findings worth keeping:
 
 - The original init table (`$003B`) sets VDP register 6 to `$FB`, so sprite
   tiles come from VRAM `$0000`. SMSlib defaults to `$2000` (the boot font), so
   `screen_game_screen_load()` writes `$FB` to register 6.
 - The original VBlank handler keeps interrupts disabled until its final `ei`. SMSlib
   helpers such as `SMS_VRAMmemcpy` re-enable them, which let a line interrupt hit the
   middle of the display-off screen draw and drop name-table cells (black tiles) and,
   later, corrupt VDP registers (the player sprite turned into font letters). The
   frame handler in `game_screen.c` therefore uses plain port writes only.
 - `dev/crt0_sms.s` is the devkitSMS startup file with one change: it clears work
   RAM (`$C000-$DEEE`). The stock file clears only `l__DATA` bytes from `$C000`, which
   missed SMSlib's variables (handler pointers) once `--data-loc` moved to `$C620`.
   That worked on emulators that zero RAM but halted on Emulicious and would on
   hardware. Check with a random-RAM start when changing startup code.
 - ROM addresses used as literals (`$2B49`, `$2C0B`, and the inline enemy animation
   tables such as `$1FD6`, listed in `DATA_POINTERS`) are rewritten to symbols by
   the converter, since the code is relocated. Leaving them as numbers made enemies
   read random ROM bytes and hung the game.
 - `ihx2sms` warns when the ROM exceeds 32 KB; check the `_GSINIT` area in
   `build/transbot.map` ends below `$7FF0`, which `tests/test_rom_assets.py` also checks.
 - `make test` also checks the stage streams inside the built ROM against the
   original and runs the original decoders and scroll setup in `sz80`.

 """Check the banked stage streams in the actual built cartridge image."""
 
 from pathlib import Path
 import re
 import unittest
 
 
 ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
 
 
 class RomAssetTests(unittest.TestCase):
     def test_rom_is_32k_with_intact_header(self):
         rom = (ROOT / "build/transbot.sms").read_bytes()
         self.assertEqual(len(rom), 0x8000)
         self.assertEqual(rom[0x7FF0:0x7FF8], b"TMR SEGA")
 
     def test_stage_streams_match_original_rom(self):
         rom = (ROOT / "build/transbot.sms").read_bytes()
         original = (ROOT / "../TransbotASM/TransBot.sms").read_bytes()
         link_map = (ROOT / "build/transbot.map").read_text()
         for symbol, start, end in (
             ("_stage_map", 0x4446, 0x4957),
             ("_stage_tiles", 0x5116, 0x58F6),
         ):
             with self.subTest(symbol=symbol):
                 match = re.search(rf"^\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s+{symbol}\s", link_map, re.MULTILINE)
                 self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"{symbol} missing from linker map")
                 address = int(match.group(1), 16)
                 self.assertLess(address + end - start, 0x7FF0)
                 self.assertEqual(rom[address:address + end - start], original[start:end])
